_comment: Offline fallback knowledge base used by scripts/build_db.py when the public dataset cannot be downloaded. Symptom phrases are deliberately lay-friendly so transcribed speech embeds close to them. Extend freely or replace with the full dataset.

conditions.name: Common Cold
conditions.description: A mild, self-limiting viral infection of the nose and throat, most often caused by rhinoviruses. Symptoms build over one to two days and usually resolve within a week to ten days.
precautions: Rest and stay hydrated
Wash hands often to avoid spreading the virus
Use saline drops or steam inhalation for congestion
See a doctor if fever lasts more than 3 days or breathing becomes difficult

conditions.name: Influenza
conditions.icd11_title: Influenza due to identified seasonal influenza virus
conditions.description: A viral infection of the respiratory tract caused by influenza viruses. Onset is typically sudden, with high fever and body aches, and it differs from the common cold by its severity.
symptoms: muscle aches all over the body
precautions: Rest and drink plenty of fluids
Stay home to avoid infecting others
Annual flu vaccination is the best prevention
Seek urgent care for shortness of breath, chest pain, or persistent high fever

conditions.name: Allergic Rhinitis
conditions.description: An allergic reaction in the nose triggered by pollen, dust mites, mold, or animal dander. Symptoms flare on exposure and can be seasonal or year-round.
precautions: Identify and avoid the trigger where possible
Antihistamines relieve symptoms
Keep windows closed during high pollen days
See a doctor if symptoms interfere with sleep or daily life

conditions.name: Bronchial Asthma
conditions.description: A chronic inflammatory disease of the airways in which they narrow and swell in response to triggers such as allergens, exercise, cold air, or infection, causing episodes of reversible breathing difficulty.
symptoms: dry cough, often worse at night
precautions: Carry the prescribed reliever inhaler at all times
Identify and avoid personal triggers
Follow the written asthma action plan from your doctor
Seek emergency care if the inhaler does not relieve breathlessness or speech is difficult

conditions.name: Migraine
conditions.description: A primary headache disorder marked by recurrent moderate-to-severe throbbing headaches, often one-sided and aggravated by movement, frequently with nausea and sensitivity to light and sound.
symptoms: visual aura such as flashing lights
precautions: Rest in a dark, quiet room at onset
Track triggers such as poor sleep, stress, and certain foods
Take prescribed medication early in the attack
Seek urgent care for the worst headache of your life, or headache with fever, stiff neck, confusion, or weakness

conditions.name: Acute Gastroenteritis
conditions.icd11_title: Infectious gastroenteritis or colitis of presumed infectious origin
conditions.description: Infection or irritation of the stomach and intestines, usually viral, causing sudden diarrhea and vomiting. Most cases settle in a few days; dehydration is the main risk.
precautions: Rehydrate with oral rehydration solution in small frequent sips
Eat bland, light foods as tolerated
Wash hands carefully and disinfect surfaces
Seek care for blood in stool, signs of dehydration, or diarrhea lasting more than 3 days

conditions.name: Gastroesophageal Reflux Disease
conditions.description: A chronic condition in which stomach acid flows back into the esophagus because the valve between them weakens, producing heartburn and irritation. Often worsens after large meals or when lying down.
symptoms: heartburn, a burning feeling behind the breastbone
acid or food coming back up
worse symptoms when lying down or bending over
precautions: Eat smaller meals and avoid eating late at night
Limit spicy foods, alcohol, caffeine, and fatty meals
Raise the head of the bed
See a doctor for frequent symptoms, difficulty swallowing, or unexplained weight loss

conditions.name: Urinary Tract Infection
conditions.description: Bacterial infection of the bladder and lower urinary tract, far more common in women. It causes painful, urgent urination; untreated it can spread upward to the kidneys.
symptoms: frequent urge to urinate, passing only small amounts
precautions: Drink plenty of water
Do not hold urine; empty the bladder fully
See a doctor for a urine test and antibiotics if symptoms persist
Seek urgent care for fever, back pain, or vomiting, which suggest kidney involvement

conditions.name: Essential Hypertension
conditions.description: Persistently raised blood pressure without a single identifiable secondary cause. Usually silent for years, it is a major risk factor for heart disease, stroke, and kidney damage.
symptoms: headaches, especially at the back of the head in the morning
discovered on routine blood pressure checks
precautions: Reduce salt intake and eat more fruit and vegetables
Exercise regularly and keep a healthy weight
Limit alcohol and stop smoking
Monitor blood pressure and take prescribed medication daily; seek care for readings above 180/120 with symptoms

conditions.name: Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus
conditions.description: A metabolic disorder in which the body resists insulin or does not make enough of it, so blood glucose stays high. It develops gradually and is strongly linked to weight and inactivity.
symptoms: tingling or numbness in hands and feet
precautions: Follow a balanced, low-sugar diet and exercise plan
Take prescribed medication or insulin consistently
Check blood glucose as advised and keep appointments
Seek urgent care for very high glucose with vomiting, confusion, or fruity-smelling breath

conditions.name: Pneumonia
conditions.description: Infection that inflames the air sacs of one or both lungs, which may fill with fluid. Bacterial pneumonia often follows a cold or flu and can become serious, especially in the young and elderly.
symptoms: cough with green, yellow, or bloody phlegm
sharp chest pain that is worse when breathing or coughing
precautions: See a doctor promptly; antibiotics are needed for bacterial pneumonia
Rest and drink plenty of fluids
Complete the full course of prescribed antibiotics
Seek emergency care for blue lips, severe breathlessness, or chest pain

conditions.name: Dengue
conditions.description: A mosquito-borne viral infection common in tropical regions. Fever is typically high and sudden, with severe body aches; the dangerous phase comes as fever falls, when plasma can leak.
symptoms: mild bleeding such as nose or gum bleeds
precautions: Use paracetamol; avoid aspirin and ibuprofen, which raise bleeding risk
Drink plenty of fluids
Watch for warning signs as fever falls: severe abdominal pain, repeated vomiting, bleeding, restlessness
Get urgent hospital care if warning signs appear
